pairs.subject: client-fetch-cache
pairs.evidence: examples/atlas/data/index.ts:97 The only cache in this context is LENS_CACHE, a module-private derive cache behind the single public door lensFor, keyed by concept id over static compiled data. It admits only known concepts and holds at most one entry per concept, so the parse-and-derive obligations hold. The network techniques have no fetch layer to apply to: a search of all of examples/atlas for fetch(, useSWR, useQuery and staleTime found nothing.

techniques.evidence: examples/atlas/data/index.ts:97 lensFor is the only way in, and LENS_CACHE (line 89) is not exported. The derivation is pure over immutable bundle data. It caches no failures: unknown ids return NO_LENS without being stored. The mutation assumption is stated at the module head (line 4, 'PURE'), not at the cache line.

examples/atlas/data/index.ts:99 The key is conceptId, the only thing that changes the answer. The model is compiled into the bundle and never changes at runtime, so there is no hidden input. Every bundle starts with an empty module cache, so changing the logic leaves no old entries to serve.

examples/atlas/data/index.ts:94 The reason for reuse is written at the construction site: it is read on every render and needs stable set identity. Line 102 refuses to admit unknown ids, so the number of entries is capped by the static concept list.
examples/atlas/app/page.tsx:4 There is no server-owned data, so nothing can go stale and there is no freshness window to design.
examples/atlas/lib/constants.ts:4 No request is ever in flight, so there is nothing to deduplicate.
examples/atlas/lib/constants.ts:5 The data lives at module scope by construction, so a remount is always warm without any fetched-result cache.
examples/atlas/app/page.tsx:5 The page is static and has no loads to prefetch or defer.

pairs.registryProposal: The golden path's precondition ('a client that talks to an authority') does not cover a client whose only cache is a pure derive cache over data compiled into the bundle. A context-level not-applicable is impossible here because the word 'cache' appears, yet 8 of the 11 techniques cannot apply. The standard could state that a bundle-static client is judged on parse-and-derive-caches, cache-key-discipline and admission-hypothesis only.
